source.title: DUSK: Do Not Unlearn Shared Knowledge
source.authors: Wonje Jeung; Sangyeon Yoon; Hyesoo Hong; Soeun Kim; Seungju Han; Youngjae Yu; Albert No

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether unlearning removes targeted knowledge while retaining other capabilities, and reports that the tested methods often leave substantial unique-forget knowledge. Its results refine the scope of claims about successful unlearning, but it does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates unlearning outcomes on its own synthetic benchmark. It does not test relearning, activation ablation, quantization, or prompt-based recovery. Verbatim-memorization, shared-knowledge, unique-retain, and distributional metrics are not included as rows here because they do not measure the targeted-knowledge accuracy or general downstream capability specified in version A. The abstract and cited prior-work discussion are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: The study measures residual forget-only knowledge (UFK) and general capability after nine unlearning configurations on LLaMA-3-8B. This bears directly on version A's claim of near-complete removal with preserved ability. It applies no recovery attacks, so versions B–F are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that most methods remove verbatim text but largely fail to erase forget-specific facts without also damaging shared knowledge. They add that general downstream ability is mostly preserved, and that no method fully removes Df's influence while preserving behaviour on Dr.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates established unlearning configurations on a synthetic multi-source overlap benchmark; it does not reproduce the original studies' recovery attacks or attack measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The method configurations yield different UFK and downstream capability values; TAU has a notable downstream-capability drop. Unlearning was stopped at the first epoch when URK fell below 70.

fits_no_version.finding: Membership-inference Privacy Leakage (Min-K%++) shows over-unlearning for most methods and under-unlearning for NPO (−45.0) and RMU (−98.6). Retain Deviation exceeds 5% for all methods except RMU.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distributional traces of the forget set (detectable by MIA) persist or are over-suppressed after unlearning, independent of QA accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Verbatim memorization is strongly suppressed (TAU ROUGE-L F1 0.125 vs Target 0.638), while unique facts remain answerable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning removes surface text more readily than underlying facts.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 2025
record.problems: The benchmark uses synthetic professor data and one model family, LLaMA-3-8B. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper does not apply any of the recovery attacks specified in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's verbatim-memorization metrics, shared and unique retain scores, privacy leakage, retain deviation, and individual downstream task scores were not extracted as rows because they do not directly measure the targeted-knowledge accuracy or general downstream-capability aggregate in version A; no recovery-attack results are reported.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge; no attack is applied.
No activation ablation and no analysis of blocking versus deletion.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, cross-lingual or in-context recovery.
No new method is proposed, and robustness to attacks is not tested.

missing.what: Collateral loss of shared knowledge (SK, −25% to −66% vs Retrain) and unique retain knowledge (URK, −18% to −40%). This is a cost to knowledge adjacent to the forget set that the DC average does not show.
UFK vs SK trajectories over epochs: pushing UFK lower costs shared knowledge (trade-off region).
Per-task downstream scores, e.g. GSM8K falls to 0.125 (GA) and 0.112 (TAU) vs 0.268 Retrain.

record.verdict_notes: Single model (LLaMA-3-8B), synthetic professor data, no uncertainty reported. The residual UFK is measured by direct QA, not recovered by an attack, so the study bears on A's 'near chance' clause, not on the shallow-unlearning attack versions. UFK levels depend on the utility-matched stopping rule (URK<70; epochs per method in Table 4), which is why the verdict is limits_scope rather than challenges.

versions.untested_parts: The paper measures unique-forget knowledge and downstream capability, but does not test whether simple attacks recover knowledge after unlearning.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack is applied.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocked access versus deletion is reported.
No prompt-rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack is applied.
The paper evaluates nine unlearning configurations, but does not test resistance to the attacks in versions B–E.

tranche.reason: Authors argue that current methods leave forget-specific facts and also harm shared knowledge, so version A is partial. This fits T5; T3 (new setting) is also arguable.

source_check.notes: All UFK and DC values match Table 1 and Table 7; the column order survives in the text. Only version A is tested; no recovery attacks were run. The paper's own text in App. C.2 says GA and GAGD average above 0.40, but Table 7 gives 0.3753 and 0.3898; use the table. Fig. 3c (RMU at 50 epochs) shows that longer unlearning can reach ideal Df scores at the risk of Dr collapse.

statements.correction: DUSK LLaMA-3-8B, stopped at first epoch with URK < 70: RMU DC 39.1 vs Retrain 40.6, but RMU UFK 55.1 vs Retrain 5.2 (Target 83.8). Forgetting is incomplete.
statements.problem: Cites DC-RMU from DUSK but gives no DUSK numbers. DUSK does not show forgetting to retrain level (RMU is its weakest forgetter), so it backs only the utility half.

statements.correction: Nine configurations. DC is 37.5-40.3 for GA, GAGD, GAKL, NPO, NPOGD, NPOKL, RMU and TV, and 35.8 for TAU, vs Retrain 40.6. GA DC 37.5; UFK GA 24.3, NPO 43.0 vs Retrain 5.2.
statements.problem: 'All eight configurations score 37.5-40.3' is wrong: DUSK runs nine configurations, and TAU (left out) scores 35.8, a -12% drop. GA and NPO values are right.
